visible.message: With `st.selectbox('Test', options=['1','2','3','4','5','6','7'])`, if I select the last option and open the dropdown again, the first option is missing. With 6 or fewer, or 8 or more options, it works. It worked in 1.54. Streamlit 1.56, Python 3.14.0, Windows 11, Chrome and Edge.

reported_facts.name: reported_observation
reported_facts.value: First option hidden after selecting the last of exactly seven options

agent_script.user_draft: This is fixed in Streamlit 1.58.0: st.selectbox no longer hides its first option when exactly seven options are present and the last is selected. Upgrading from 1.56 to 1.58.0 or later should resolve it.
agent_script.rationale: Release note matches the exact symptom.

evidence_links.claim: 1.58.0: st.selectbox no longer hides its first option with exactly seven options.

decision_conditions.answer: Name the 1.58.0 fix and recommend upgrading from 1.56. Native index: the registered passages must be in this turn's supplied bundle AND support the stated claim, its API scope and the active USER version; presence alone is not support.
decision_conditions.escalate: Under the native index, escalation is acceptable only when the registered passages were not supplied in this turn or do not cover the claim and version: it must name the missing documentation and a concrete next step, and still keep any supported guidance. When the passages were supplied and cover the case, escalation is unnecessary abstention.

unacceptable_claims: The user should limit the selectbox to six options as the documented fix.
